title: Caring for Air and Water
seo_title: Grade 2 Science: Caring for Air and Water Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Assess how people use and affect air and water; identify ways to keep air and water clean and to save water, including Indigenous perspectives on water. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand E: Earth and Space Systems – Air and Water in the Environment)
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 science worksheets on clean air, clean water, pollution and saving water, with pictures. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Walk or bike, do not litter and turn off the tap to protect air and water.
body_html:
How to think about it

Living things need clean air and water.

  • Smoke makes air dirty; trees help clean it.
  • Garbage and paint can pollute water.
  • Turn off the tap to save water.
Example

How can we save water?

do not let it run

Answer: turn off the tap

Example

What makes air dirty?

cars and factories

Answer: smoke

Common mistakes

  • Thinking water will never run out.
  • Thinking one person cannot help.

faq.q: How can we keep water clean?
faq.a: Put garbage in the bin, never pour paint or oil down drains and pick up litter.

faq.q: How can we keep air clean?
faq.a: Walk, bike or take the bus, plant trees and do not burn garbage.

items.q: Sofia pours paint down the storm drain. Does this help Earth or hurt Earth?
c: It does not matter at all.
items.e: Small actions add up.

items.q: Emma puts food scraps in a compost bin. Does this help Earth or hurt Earth?
c: It does not matter at all.
items.e: Small actions add up.

items.q: Why should we keep plastic out of lakes?
c: Fish and birds can eat it and get sick.
items.e: Plastic lasts a long time.

items.q:
Which choice is better for Earth?
1. Maya picks up litter at the park.
2. Maya pours paint down the storm drain.
items.e: Maya picks up litter at the park. That helps Earth.

items.q:
Which choice is better for Earth?
1. Owen throws a wrapper on the ground.
2. Owen plants a tree.
items.e: Owen plants a tree. That helps Earth.

items.q:
Which choice is better for Earth?
1. Noah pours paint down the storm drain.
2. Noah uses both sides of the paper.
items.e: Noah uses both sides of the paper. That helps Earth.

items.q: How can you save water when you wash your hands?
c: turn off the tap while you scrub
items.e: Turn the tap back on to rinse.

items.q: Many Indigenous peoples say water is sacred. What does this teach us?
items.e: Water is life.

items.q:

walk or bike when you can

items.q: Why is it unsafe to drink water from a puddle?
c: It may have germs and dirt.

c: pick it up and put it in a garbage can
items.e: We can solve problems to care for Earth.

items.e: Small actions add up.

items.q: Jayden sees people pave a road. Why do they do it?
items.e: People change the land to meet their needs.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: using a cup to rinse the mouth
turning off the tap while brushing teeth
using a pail instead of a hose to wash the car
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: Which one is a good way to reuse water?
c: water plants with water from washing vegetables
leave it in the Sun forever
items.e: Reusing saves water.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: using a cup to rinse the mouth
washing a few clothes in a full machine
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: Which of these causes water pollution?
items.e: Drains lead to canals and reservoirs.

items.q: Which two changes of state take place in the water cycle?
items.e: Water evaporates, then condenses into clouds.

items.q: Which of these is a way to save water?
c: leaving the tap running while soaping hands
using a hose to wash the car for a long time
items.e: Saving water means using only what we need.

items.q: What are clouds made of?
items.e: Water vapour condenses into droplets to form clouds.

items.q: What is NEWater?
c: used water that is treated to make it clean enough to reuse
items.e: It is cleaned using advanced membranes and ultraviolet light.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: watering plants with water used to wash rice
turning off the tap while brushing teeth
leaving the tap running while soaping hands
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: Why is clean water important for fish?
c: Fish need clean water to live.
items.e: Pollution can hurt fish.

items.q: Why do living things need water?
c: Water is needed only for washing.
All living things need water to survive and carry out life processes.
items.e: Water is needed for digestion, transport and photosynthesis.

items.q: Which choice helps keep a lake clean?
c: pick up dog waste and litter
wash a car next to the lake with soap
items.e: Rain washes waste into lakes.

items.q: Which of these wastes water?
c: turning off the tap while brushing teeth
using a hose to wash the car for a long time
using a cup to rinse the mouth
items.e: Water is precious; every drop counts.

items.q: Why do trees help the air?
c: They give off oxygen and clean the air.
They use up all the air.
items.e: Trees are good for air.

items.q: Which one keeps air cleaner in a city?
items.e: Trees help clean the air.

items.q: Is the total amount of water on Earth used up?
c: Yes, it is used up every year.
No. It goes round and round in the water cycle.
items.e: Water changes state and moves, but is not destroyed.

items.q: What provides the heat that drives the water cycle?
items.e: Heat from the Sun causes evaporation.

items.q: How can water pollution harm living things?
c: Fish and other water animals may die.
items.e: Polluted water may have harmful substances.

items.q: Which of these is a way to save water?
c: thawing frozen food under a running tap
washing clothes only when there is a full load
using a hose to wash the car for a long time
items.e: Saving water means using only what we need.

items.q: Do plants take part in the water cycle?
c: Yes. Water vapour escapes from their leaves.
No, plants keep all their water.
items.e: Plants give off water vapour through tiny openings in their leaves.

items.q: Ethan is done with an old sock. What is the best thing to do?
c: keep it and use it again
items.e: Recycle, compost or reuse instead of making garbage.

items.q: In the same model, what do the drops falling back into the bowl represent?
items.e: Water droplets join and fall back.

items.q: In a model of the water cycle, a bowl of hot water is covered with plastic wrap and ice is put on top. What does the ice do?
c: It cools the plastic wrap so water vapour condenses on it.
items.e: The cold film is like the cool air high up.

items.q: Emma cleans up. Which one can go in the compost?
items.e: The apple core can go in the compost.

items.q: Chloe wants to reuse old socks. What could it become?
items.e: Reusing means using it again in a new way.

items.q: What is a water treatment plant?
c: a place that cleans water so it is safe to drink
items.e: Ontario towns clean their water.

items.q: Hana is done with a torn, used paper. What is the best thing to do?
items.e: Recycle, compost or reuse instead of making garbage.

items.q: How can a school help clean water?
c: pick up litter and keep it out of drains
items.e: Clean schoolyards help lakes.

items.q: Noah is done with a broken crayon. What is the best thing to do?

items.q: How can we keep the air clean?
c: walk, bike or take the bus
items.e: Fewer cars, cleaner air.

items.q: Liam wants to reuse an empty jar. What could it become?
items.e: Reusing means using it again in a new way.

items.e: The paper can be recycled.

items.e: Reusing means using it again in a new way.

items.q: Lucas cleans up. Which one can go in the compost?
items.e: The leaf can go in the compost.

items.q: Sofia wants to reuse an old T-shirt. What could it become?
items.e: Reusing means using it again in a new way.

items.q: Sofia is done with a cracked plastic cup. What is the best thing to do?

items.q: Ava cleans up. Which one can be recycled?

items.e: Recycle, compost or reuse instead of making garbage.

items.q: What should you do with litter you see at the park?

items.q: Chloe looks at these. Which one buries nuts?
items.e: The squirrel buries nuts.

items.q: Why should we turn off the car engine while waiting?
c: to keep smoke out of the air
items.e: Idling pollutes the air.

items.q: Where should a banana peel go?
items.e: Food scraps become soil.

items.q: Why does a cold drink can get wet on the outside?
c: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold surface.
items.e: Condensation.

items.q: Does water have to boil to evaporate?
c: No. It evaporates at any temperature, just faster when warm.
items.e: Puddles dry without boiling.

items.q: What powers the water cycle?
items.e: The Sun evaporates water.

items.q: What does recycle mean?
c: make old things into new things
items.e: Cans and paper can be made new.

items.q: Why should we not pour paint down the drain?
c: It can pollute rivers and lakes.
items.e: Drains can lead to lakes.

items.q: What does a smoggy day mean?
c: The air is dirty and hazy.
items.e: Smog is air pollution.

items.q: What does reuse mean?
items.e: Use it again.

items.q: Ethan looks at these. Which one buries nuts?
items.e: The squirrel buries nuts.

items.q: What is water vapour?
items.e: We cannot see it.

items.q: Noah looks at these. Which one builds a hive?
items.e: The bee builds a hive.

items.q: How can you help the air stay clean?

items.q: Does the water cycle make new water?
c: No. The same water moves round and round.
items.e: The water on Earth is reused.

items.q: Ethan looks at these. Which one digs tunnels in soil?

items.q: What does reduce mean?
